newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government bows to hostage-takers' demands.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government bows to hostage-takers' demands.

text.p: The Tajik government said on Tuesday it would bow to the demands of a rebel group holding several United Nations officials hostage by allowing the return of fellow rebels from Afghanistan to the ex-Soviet republic.

"At an urgent meeting held by (Tajik President Imomali) Rakhmonov in Dushanbe, the government has agreed to implement the fighters' demands," Rakhmonov's spokesman, Zafar Saidov, said by telephone. "Active negotiations are under way."
But he added that the method of exchange, and whether the 40 rebels in northern Afghanistan would be allowed to return with their weapons, had still to be decided.

Tajik rebel leader Rizvon Sadirov returned home from Afghanistan on Monday to help negotiate the release of hostages held by his brother Bakhrom, but appeared to offer little assistance once he arrived.
Rizvon Sadirov is now reported to be at his brother's base near the town of Obigarm in a mountainous area 80 km (50 miles) east of the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

The hostage crisis began early last week when Bakhrom's rebels seized four United Nations military observers. They later captured a carload of Russian reporters and four workers with the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR.
The crisis worsened on Saturday when the rebels seized Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukharov who had flown in to negotiate with the hostage-takers.
Daily announcements by the government saying the hostages would be released have been dashed repeatedly while the rebels have ignored appeals from international organisations.
The government has said it would not use force to secure the hostages' release.
The hostage crisis comes just as the government and Islamist opposition rebels are trying to end a bitter four-year civil war that has left tens of thousands dead and many more homeless.
Saidov said the president had spoken to opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri on Tuesday and that both had agreed the kidnappings were "targeted against the process of reconciliation".
Rakhmonov and Nuri agreed on a ceasefire at a meeting in northern Afghanistan last December which appears to be holding.
Saidov said the two had agreed to hold a summit in the near future but gave no further details. A further round of peace talks is planned for February 26 in Moscow.
